reasoning: iter-033: pack colors into GaussianCullRec (extended from 40B to 64B cache-line-aligned). Hypothesis: blend's per-(g, mb) inner loop does two random fetches (gauss_rec + colors); collapsing into one cache line halves blend memory-fetch count. Result: REGRESSION. blend p50 5.30 -> 5.40 ms; sum_total 341 -> 357 ms (+5%). Project also slightly slower (2.94 -> 3.12). PSNR bit-identical (60.33 / 63.26) so algorithm is correct. Root cause: the 64B record bloats gauss_rec from 9.4 MB (40B * 234k) to 15.0 MB (64B * 234k), which exceeds the M-Pro's 16 MB shared L2. The previous 9.4 MB working set fit L2 comfortably; now we spill to main memory on every random fetch for both cull AND blend. Save on blend (eliminate 65k separate colors fetches) is overwhelmed by the extra L2 misses across 294k cull fetches. Reverting. Lesson: gauss_rec size is bounded by L2 capacity; future packing experiments must keep total <= 12 MB. Alternative: split colors into its own array with tighter (e.g. fp16) packing, or compute SH0 -> RGB on-the-fly from a smaller representation.
